main_text.p: subsunt, sed in magni Imperatoris nostri, & ex-celsi dispositionem, atque iudicium, illa illius cura, ac prouidentia demandamus. Et Photius τοσούτων μηχανορράφων κακῶν[?] eadem ipsa secunda Actione. Φῶν@[?] ὁ ἀγωνιστὴς Πα-[?] ζιαφῆς[?] ἄπιστος[?]. Οὐ ζῶ πεισαίω[?], ὲ ἐνδίσῳ[?] λόγῳ πε-[?] ιέχει[?], καὶ εἰς τὸ ἡμέτερον ἀὐτ[illegible, ~6 letters] ἐμ[illegible, ~4 letters] τὸ τέλος, καὶ σοφῆς, καὶ ἀποδοχῆς ἀξία νομίζομεν.

Quæ decenti, ac iusta rationi in nituntur, & ad nostram mediocritatem pertinent, & opus illorum, & absolutio, digna, quæ recipiantur existimamus. Subit modo Achillæum illud apud Euripidem in Iphigenia in Aulide. Nanque cum propositiet illi Chorus, obediendum esse Principibus, qui ratione, & experientia edocti, recte vitam agunt cum prudentia, non negat Achilles obediendum, sed si præerunt recte, & vtiliter sapient: sin minus, parendum illis non esse.

Καὶ τοῖς Ἀτρείδαις, ὧ μὲν ἡγῶνται καλῶς[?] Πεισόμεθ᾽[?], ὅταν ἡ μὴ καλῶς ἡγῶνται[?]. Proin Atridis, si probi fuerint duces; parebimus, sin improbi, haud parebimus. Hac eadem ratione Photius, & Synodus obtemperant Pontifici Romano, si iusta, & canonica præcipiat: sin minus, parere nolunt. Quis porro iudex erit de iustitia, & iniustitia mandatorum? Synodus ipsa, & Photius.

page.notes: Greek text is faint and partly illegible in the scan; the Greek words marked [?] and the bracketed gaps are uncertain readings. The first Greek line of the quotation, and the word after Φῶν, could not be read with confidence. The Greek 'ω' rendered as '@' in one place is an uncertain character. The page ends mid-sentence, with the catchword "Et" below the last line. Printed hyphens kept as printed: "ex-celsi", "Pa-", "pe-".
